text.p: Thousands of volunteers fanned out in Bangladesh's coastal areas on Sunday to prepare for possible mass evacuations as a cyclone moved in from the Bay of Bengal.
Weather officials said the storm, with winds up to 200 kph (120 mph), may hit the coast by early Monday.
They said waves of up to four metres (12 ft) could swamp widespread coastal areas.
Fishermen have been warned not to leave port and coastal officials had been told to hoist danger signals.
According to a latest bulletin from the Storm Warning Centre the cyclone was located 600 km (375 miles) south southwest of Chittagong port city at 9 a.m. (0300 GMT) on Sunday.
"It's definitely approaching towards the coast," said a weather official.

"The storm is advancing at a speed of 25 kph (16 miles). The speed may gather momentum and in that case the storm is expected to hit the coast after midnight," Amirul Hussain, regional director of the Meteorological Department, told Reuters.
Abdul Wahab, a Bangladesh Red Crescent field official, said some 30,000 trained volunteers had been deployed in coastal districts, mainly Chittagong and Cox's Bazar.
"They have been asked to closely monitor the situation and standby for a large scale evacuation work," he said.
Officials at the Chittagong port said some 24 ships, now berthed at jetties, would be moved soon to outer anchorages.
"We are taking this precaution so the ships do not collide during the storm and jam the channel by sinking," said Quamrul Islam, Harbour Master of Chittagong port.
Bangladesh's worst cyclone in 1991 killed more than 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
